missing_units.reason: No unit checks whether storage can trust a caller's content_hash, and the render dedup is keyed only by that hash. Source facts. (1) entry.py:225-244 measures content_hash only when data is not None or source=='text'. So Entry(path='/x.pdf', source='bytes', data=None, content_hash=H) validates and keeps the caller's H. entry.py:208-213 and 542-548 also let model_validate(context={MEASURED_BODY: BodyMetrics}) vouch any hash for real data. (2) base.py:2633-2645 (_route_entry_batch) accepts caller Entry objects after an isinstance check and the path gate only. writes.py:160-171 and 1172 store entry.content_hash as given. writes.py:987 gives a bodiless row no content or blob row, and writes.py:1181 marks it render_status='pending'. (3) The operator's reindex selects that row (render.py:165-176). cached_renderings (render.py:184-238) picks the lowest-id settled donor per (content_hash, generation) anywhere in the mount, with no owner, principal or rights predicate. render_rows (render.py:283-289) uses the cached rendering without needing the row's blob. land_renderings (render.py:336-343) guards only that the receiving row still holds content_hash == H. So the donor's rendered text is written into the attacker's own row, and the attacker reads it back with read. In the reverse direction, a planted row with attacker bytes and a vouched hash H becomes the donor, either by having the lowest id or as the first twin in a page (render_rows seen-dict). A victim's later upload with hash H then gets attacker-chosen derived text, and grep, glean and chunks are built from it. The same key also drives the cross-mount glean dedup (rerank.py:274-278, first mount keeps the row), so a forged hash on an earlier mount can suppress another principal's hit. It also drives the version-mint skip (versions.py:146). The hunter must settle one open question: how a lower-trust principal gets H. LIST_FIELDS is path and kind only (reads.py:107). Ways to get it include a prior read, a publicly known document, or the render_status difference as a membership oracle for a guessed H. The hunter must also confirm the full write -> reindex -> read lineage on InMemoryStorage. No existing candidate fingerprint touches content_hash, render dedup or caller-authored metrics. The rendering unit's checks cover parser cost and units_from_json only.

graph meet minimal=True unit (reassigned, not resolved) :: why it is reassigned. Source sets an upper bound. prune (graph.py:422-440) rebuilds _adjacency over all walk.edges and reruns _articulation_points once for each removed node, with no budget or offload. kept is at most seeds + 2*(seeds-1)*depth_reached. Whether a caller can make the removable count grow with corpus size decides between candidate and hardening, and source does not settle that. A sketch suggests it can. Use a hub seed H with children c_i, take seeds s_i through observations= (no seed cap, backend.py:433), and add rejected-meeting edges s_i-c_{i+1}, which walk.see() keeps (graph.py:384). That makes c_i non-articulation, giving about m removals over O(m) edges. The hunter should confirm this with _adjacency and _articulation_points call counts at m and 2m on InMemoryStorage.
